nodes.name: NF Pretreatment and NiFe-LDH Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: Initially, a piece of NF (2 cm×3 cm) was subjected to ultrasonic pretreatment using acetone, dilute hydrochloric acid, deionized water, and anhydrous ethanol successively. Next, NF was subjected to freeze-drying. Following this, a uniform solution was created by introducing a 1:1 molar ratio of nickel nitrate hexahydrate and iron nitrate nonahydrate, alongside 2.5 mmol of urea and 2 mmol of ammonium fluoride, into 20 mL of deionized water while employing magnetic stirring for a duration of 30 min. The pretreated NF was dipped into the previously mentioned solution, and this solution was moved to a Teflon reaction container and heated at 120°C for 10 h. Once the reaction concluded, the resultant product was gathered, and rinsed multiple times with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, and the samples were subsequently subjected to freeze-drying.

nodes.name: MoO3 Electrodeposition on NiFe-LDH/NF
nodes.procedure: MoO3 was deposited on NiFe-LDH through an electrodeposition method. The electrodeposition trial was performed utilizing a CHI660E electrochemical workstation under ambient temperature conditions, employing a three-electrode setup. The counter electrode was composed of a graphite rod, the reference electrode was a saturated calomel electrode (SCE), and the prepared NiFe-NF (1 cm×1 cm) was employed as the working electrode. A 1 mM ammonium molybdate solution was utilized as the electrodeposition electrolyte. Electrodeposition was carried out in the electrolyte under a specific voltage. Subsequently, the sample was washed using deionized water and then underwent freeze-drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-NF exhibits flowerball-like morphology with uniform nanosheets (lateral dimension ≈300 nm, thickness ≈10-15 nm). MoO3/NiFe-NF morphology scarcely altered after MoO3 electrodeposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1b, after the hydrothermal process, NiFe-LDH exhibited a flowerball-like morphology, with nanosheets uniformly grown onto the NF substrate. The nanosheets exhibited a lateral dimension of ≈300 nm, while their thickness measured ≈10-15 nm... The introduction of MoO3 through electrodeposition scarcely altered the morphology of the LDH nanosheets (Figure 1c,d).

nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS was further applied to examine the elemental chemical states... for NiFe-NF, the pair of peaks found at binding energies (BEs) of 712.5 and 724.6 eV...
